title: Runtime ingress backplane + serializer proto (personal notes)
content:
Goal: capture a minimal, testable API shape for the runtime ingress backplane and a compact on-wire serializer that supports low-latency partial-streaming and replay. These are notes to iterate quickly — not final.

Motivation / constraints:
- single TCP/HTTP2 connection per client-side edge to support multiplexed sessions
- compact framing to avoid per-token JSON blowup for short messages
- must support: new-session, resume-session (with delta patch), partial-stream chunks, event annotations (telemetry), strong truncated-replay markers
- backwards compatibility: header with version + capability bitmap

API shapes (high-level):
1) Control handshake (HTTP/2 HEADERS + small JSON payload)
{
  "type": "handshake",
  "client_id": "string",
  "capabilities": ["streaming", "delta-resume", "kv-cache-v2"],
  "session_hint": "opt: session-id or null",
  "keepalive_ms": 30000
}

2) Framing for payloads: 1 byte frame-type | 3 bytes length | payload
- frame-type: 0=control-json,1=chunk-binary,2=chunk-json,3=ping,4=pong,5=resume-index
- length: big-endian

3) Control JSON examples (not exhaustive):
- new-session: {"op":"new_session","meta":{...}}
- close-session: {"op":"close","reason":"client_request"}
- resume-request: {"op":"resume","resume_token":"...","desired_index": 42}

4) Chunk semantics:
- chunk-binary is raw delta-encoded token bytes (when using compact tokenizer binary format)
- chunk-json includes {"index":N,"partial":true/false,"payload":"..."}
- all chunks MUST include monotonic index for deterministic replay

ASCII topology sketch:

 client-app
    |
    | TLS + HTTP/2
    v
 edge-proxy (local) --- auth/token --- backplane (ingress)
    |                       |
    | multiplex streams      | session catalog + kv-cache
    v                       v
 runtime worker pool  <---- router / sharder

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent capability negotiation for quantization / model-variant fallback? Proposal: capability bitmap + refs to model-variant descriptors by stable id.
- Resume security model: resume token should be HMAC'd with session secret; revoke via backplane lookup. Need low-latency token revocation path.
- Telemetry: attach sparse event-annotations to chunks (small key IDs referencing schema) vs full JSON on control path. Prefer keyed annotations for perf.
- Graceful fallback: if binary tokenizer format not supported, fall back to chunk-json carrying UTF-8 tokens. Edge should advertise binary token formats it understands.

Testing plan:
- unit test: framing parser + fuzz for partial frames and misordered chunks
- integration: client emulator (python) that opens 1000 concurrent sessions over single HTTP/2 connection, runs resume cycles, ensures monotonic index enforced
- perf: measure bytes/second and median p99 latency for 8kseq streaming with binary chunks vs JSON chunks

Notes to self:
- Keep frame header minimal so proxies (envoy) can still do smart routing; avoid proprietary multipart/long headers that break observability.
- Add short compatibility header for old gateways: x-rw-backplane-v:1
- Sync with Benji on resume token HMAC algorithm (HS256 vs KMAC) and with Marta for telemetry annotation ids

Quick sketch of resume token lifecycle:
1) server issues token: base64(session_id || ':' || index || ':' || hmac)
2) client stores, includes on resume
3) backplane validates via session catalog cache; if missing, forward to runtime-store (authoritative), then cache result

Open doc links: reference binary tokenizer spec (TODO embed small example), token-indexing proof-of-concept in github PR 428.

End of notes. Will iterate into a proto/IDL if this shape stabilizes after perf runs and security review.
